title: CRLR/724/2019 of AJAY AGARWAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
CRLR No. 724 of 2019
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mrs. Neetu Singh, Advocate for the revisionist.
Mr. P.S. Bohra, AGA for the State.
The respondent-wife i.e. (respondent No. 2 herein) had
instituted an application under Section 125 Cr.PC for the grant
of maintenance by filing the same on 17.12.2018, before the
Court of Additional Family Judge, Roorkee, District Haridwar.
The said application, which was instituted as Criminal Case No.
304 of 2018, Smt. Parul Agarwal and others v. Ajay Agarwal,
the same is pending consideration before the said Family Court.
In the proceedings before the learned Family Court,
respondent No. 2 had filed an application under sub Section (2)
of Section 125 Cr.PC, for the grant of interim maintenance for
herself, as well as, for her daughter i.e. respondent No. 3 herein.
The learned Family Court, while passing the impugned order
dated 24.10.2019, had determined the interim maintenance as
payable to respondent No. 2 i.e. the wife @ Rs. 5,000/- per
month and to the respondent No. 3 i.e. the daughter @ Rs.
10,000/- per month that means an overall amount of Rs.
15,000/- payable to the respondent.
The argument of the learned counsel for the revisionist
is that the said amount is too excessive and it is an excessive
from the view point that the same is directed to be paid from the
date of application itself. The learned counsel for the revisionist
submits that though it is an admitted case that the revisionist is
working in a Central School, and out of the said engagement, he
is having an income of about Rs. 15,35,000/- per annum.
Learned counsel for the revisionist further submits that since
there is a possibility of an amicable settlement between the
parties, and which is not being progressed before the Court
below, an appropriate effort for mediation could be made before
the High Court itself.
While considering the revision itself on its own merits,
and also taking into consideration the rival pleadings about the
income, accruing to the revisionist, this Court is of the view that
the amount of interim maintenance, which has been determined
@ Rs. 15,000/- per month, by way of a consolidated amount of
maintenance for respondent Nos. 2 and 3, is absolutely just and
proper, on its comparison with the income, as accruing to the
revisionist, because as per law, the determination of
maintenance, may it be even of an interim nature, it has to
commensurate with the income of the husband, so as to
maintain same standard of living as they would have been
entitled had there not been any dispute.
Even otherwise also, since the matrimony and the birth
of the daughter is an admitted fact by the revisionist, he also

owes a responsibility to maintain the wife and the daughter till
their matrimony is subsisting. The learned counsel for the
revisionist has expressed her apprehension that an effective
mediation is not possible in the Family Court of Roorkee and as
such, in case if the revision is entertained, and efforts for
mediation is made by this Court, there could be a greater
possibility that the family may re-unite and discharge their
matrimonial obligations. Learned counsel for the revisionist
further submits that grant of an award of maintenance from the
date of application i.e. 17.12.2018 would be encumbering a
heavy financial liability on the revisionist.
In order to succumb the aforesaid apprehension
expressed by the revisionist, this Court is of the view that since
by the impugned order dated 24.10.2019, while deciding the
application paper No. 5B, only an interim arrangement has been
made and that is being directed to be continued only during the
pendency of Section 125 application itself, this criminal
revision is being dismissed subject to the following exceptions:-
(1) The apprehension of a failure of mediation, if it is
conducted by the Family Court is being attempted to
be eradicated by directing the District Judge, District
Haridwar himself to make an effort for mediation
within the period of two months from the date of
production of certified copy of this order and submit
his report of mediation before the Family Court.
(2) The amount of interim maintenance as directed to be
paid from the date of the application i.e. dated
17.12.2018, that is being directed to be remitted by
the revisionist to the respondent in 4 equal quarterly
installments.
(3) The amount of interim maintenance, as determined
by the learned Family Court is being directed to be
paid to respondent No.2 by 10th of each month.
(4) The learned Family Court, Tehsil Roorkee, District
Haridwar is requested to decide the main application
under Section 125 Cr.PC being Criminal Case No.
304 of 2018, Smt. Parul v. Ajay Agarwal, itself as
expeditiously as possible, but not later than 3 months
from the date of production of certified copy of this
order.
Subject to the aforesaid exceptions, the criminal revision
lacks merits hence the same stands dismissed.
